agiel.title: What an AI detector can tell you
agiel.source: Karim Ibrahim · Language Testing in Asia · 2026

scenes.label: 01 / THE FLAG
heading: A flag
is a clue.
speech: Two essays look equally polished. One was written by a learner, the other with substantial help from artificial intelligence.
If a detector flags both, what has it actually established?

scenes.label: 02 / THE EVIDENCE
heading: A review
of the evidence.
speech: Karim Ibrahim's paper is a critical literature review of AI-assisted plagiarism in second-language writing.
It selected thirty-three of fifty-seven records. Its detector results come from previous studies.

scenes.label: 03 / DETECTOR FAMILIES
heading: Four ways to look.
speech: Watermarking looks for a trace placed by a generator. A trained detector learns from examples.
Statistical methods look for patterns in text. Retrieval methods compare a passage with stored outputs.
These approaches depend on different kinds of evidence.

scenes.label: 04 / TWO ERRORS
heading: Where the flag fails.
speech: A false positive wrongly flags human writing. A false negative misses AI-generated writing.
An impressive score on one test set can hide errors when a tool faces another model, genre, or group of writers.

scenes.label: 05 / EVALUATION
heading: Judge the tool.
speech: Ibrahim proposes three questions. Is the detector reliable? Do its results generalize?
And is the tool accessible in the setting where teachers would actually use it?

scenes.label: 06 / THE DECISION
heading: A fair next step.
speech: Use a flag to decide what to investigate. Review the drafts, and give the learner a chance to explain how they wrote them.
Make the integrity decision from the evidence in context.

confessor.title: When two methods become one study
confessor.source: Johnson, Onwuegbuzie & Turner · Journal of Mixed Methods Research · 2007

scenes.label: THE QUESTION
heading: When are two methods
one study?
speech: A survey tells you how common an experience is. Interviews can help explain how people live it.
When should bringing those approaches together count as mixed methods research?

scenes.label: HOW THE DEFINITION WAS BUILT
heading: A definition
built from definitions.
speech: The three authors invited thirty-six methodologists. They analyzed nineteen definitions, some written jointly.
They compared them systematically to identify recurring ideas.

scenes.label: WHERE THE DEFINITIONS DIFFERED
heading: Five choices researchers make.
speech: The definitions differed on what gets mixed, when or where it happens, and how broad the mixing is.
They also differed on why researchers mix, and on the philosophical or practical orientation that guides their work.

scenes.label: PRIORITY OF THE STRANDS
heading: A continuum, not a ratio.
speech: A mixed study can be mainly qualitative, give the two strands equal status, or be mainly quantitative.
The lead strand reflects the purpose and design of the study.

scenes.label: THE WORKING DEFINITION
heading: Breadth. Depth.
Corroboration.
speech: The authors' general definition combines elements of qualitative and quantitative approaches.
That combination can broaden what we see, deepen what we understand, and help us check whether findings support each other.

scenes.label: WHAT REMAINS OPEN
heading: A starting point
for the field.
speech: The authors argue for mixed methods as a third paradigm. Their tentative fuller definition adds pragmatism and social awareness.
The invited group offers a starting point. Researchers still have to explain why their particular combination makes sense.

seeker.title: AI from research question to publication
seeker.source: Brady Lund, Manika Lamba & Sang Hoo Oh · arXiv preprint · 2024

scenes.label: 00 / THE ROUTE
heading: From idea
to publication.
speech: An academic paper passes through many hands. Where can artificial intelligence speed that work up?
The authors trace these possibilities in a twenty twenty-four preprint.

scenes.label: 01 / IDEA & LITERATURE
heading: Expand the search.
speech: At the research stage, a language model can suggest questions, search terms, or ways to approach unfamiliar literature.
Open the original sources before trusting a summary or citing a claim.

scenes.label: 02 / METHODS & DATA
heading: Check the method.
speech: AI can help write code or organize an analysis. Check the code, the data, and every result used in your argument.
The researcher still chooses the method and interprets the findings.

scenes.label: 03 / DRAFT & EDIT
heading: Verify the draft.
speech: Writing tools can suggest a structure, revise wording, or help a draft read more clearly.
Verify quotations and citations yourself. Follow the journal's policy for disclosing how you used the tool.

scenes.label: 04 / PEER REVIEW
heading: Screening and judgment.
speech: Editorial systems can assist with technical screening or organizing submissions.
Expert reviewers still judge the research question, the soundness of the method, and what the work contributes.
Keep confidential material within the permitted workflow.

scenes.label: 05 / PUBLICATION
heading: Who answers
for the work?
speech: The preprint describes where AI might assist and where journals would need rules. Its policy examples come from twenty twenty-four.
At every stage, people remain responsible for the claims, the evidence, and the decisions.
